answer: This patient's SOD1 p.Ala4Val variant causes a dominant toxic gain-of-function: misfolded SOD1 aggregates in motor neurons and drives degeneration [s1]. The therapeutic strategy of choice is silencing SOD1 mRNA, which removes the substrate for aggregation. Tofersen (Qalsody, BIIB067) is a SOD1-directed antisense oligonucleotide administered intrathecally [s1, s2]. In the VALOR trial, tofersen reduced CSF neurofilament light by approximately 60% at 28 weeks [s2]. Tofersen received FDA accelerated approval in April 2023 [s3].

citations.title: Miller TM et al. Trial of Antisense Oligonucleotide Tofersen for SOD1 ALS. NEJM 2020
citations.snippet: Tofersen is an antisense oligonucleotide designed to suppress SOD1 messenger RNA. SOD1 mutations cause familial ALS through a toxic gain-of-function mechanism characterized by misfolded SOD1 aggregates.

citations.title: Miller TM et al. Trial of Antisense Oligonucleotide Tofersen for SOD1 ALS (VALOR). NEJM 2022
citations.snippet: In the VALOR trial, intrathecal tofersen reduced CSF neurofilament light chain concentrations by approximately 60% from baseline at week 28 versus increases in the placebo group.

citations.title: FDA approval of Qalsody (tofersen) for SOD1-associated ALS
citations.snippet: On April 25, 2023, the FDA granted accelerated approval to Qalsody (tofersen) for the treatment of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) in adults who have a mutation in the SOD1 gene.

answer: The patient has a Duchenne deletion of DMD exon 50, which is out of frame and causes premature termination [s1]. Exon skipping that removes the adjacent exon 51 restores the reading frame and produces an internally-truncated, partially functional dystrophin resembling the Becker phenotype [s1]. Eteplirsen (Exondys 51) is a phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomer (PMO) that base-pairs with the exon 51 splice donor to induce skipping [s2]. It is approved only for patients with mutations amenable to exon-51 skipping, which is approximately 13% of DMD cases [s2]. Dystrophin restoration on biopsy is modest — typically a few percent of normal — but functional benefit on the 6-minute walk has been reported [s2].

citations.title: Mendell JR et al. Eteplirsen for the treatment of Duchenne muscular dystrophy. Annals of Neurology 2013
citations.snippet: Out-of-frame deletions disrupt translation; skipping a flanking exon (e.g., exon 51) can restore the reading frame and produce a shorter but partly functional dystrophin similar to that of the milder Becker phenotype.

citations.title: FDA Exondys 51 (eteplirsen) approval information
citations.snippet: Eteplirsen is approved for treatment of Duchenne muscular dystrophy in patients who have a confirmed mutation of the DMD gene that is amenable to exon 51 skipping. Dystrophin expression in muscle biopsies after eteplirsen treatment is increased compared to baseline.

answer: SMA type 1 is caused by homozygous loss of SMN1, with disease severity modified by SMN2 copy number; this patient has only 2 SMN2 copies [s1]. SMN2 differs from SMN1 by a single nucleotide that disrupts an exonic splicing enhancer in exon 7, so most SMN2 transcripts exclude exon 7 and yield unstable SMN [s1]. Three approved therapies should be discussed: nusinersen (Spinraza), an intrathecal ASO that promotes SMN2 exon-7 inclusion [s1]; onasemnogene abeparvovec (Zolgensma), a single-dose AAV9 gene replacement carrying SMN1 cDNA, approved for patients under 2 [s2]; and risdiplam (Evrysdi), an oral small-molecule SMN2 splicing modifier [s3]. Outcomes are strongly age-dependent — presymptomatic treatment yields the best motor trajectory.

citations.title: Finkel RS et al. Nusinersen versus Sham Control in Infantile-Onset SMA. NEJM 2017
citations.snippet: SMN2 contains a C-to-T transition that creates an exonic splicing silencer, resulting in predominantly exon-7-skipped transcript. Nusinersen is an antisense oligonucleotide that promotes exon 7 inclusion in SMN2 mRNA.

citations.title: Mendell JR et al. Single-Dose Gene-Replacement Therapy for Spinal Muscular Atrophy. NEJM 2017
citations.snippet: Onasemnogene abeparvovec is an adeno-associated virus 9 vector encoding SMN1 administered as a single intravenous infusion in infants with type 1 SMA.

citations.title: Baranello G et al. Risdiplam in Type 1 SMA (FIREFISH). NEJM 2021
citations.snippet: Risdiplam is an oral SMN2 pre-mRNA splicing modifier that increases full-length SMN protein.

answer: Huntington's disease is caused by a CAG repeat expansion in HTT producing a polyglutamine tract that confers toxic gain-of-function on huntingtin, driving aggregation and neurodegeneration [s1]. The dominant therapeutic hypothesis is lowering mutant huntingtin. Tominersen, a non-allele-selective HTT-targeting ASO from Roche, was advanced into GENERATION-HD1 but dosing was paused in March 2021 because the high-dose arm trended worse than placebo on functional outcomes [s2]. No HTT-lowering therapy is FDA-approved as of late 2025. Allele-selective approaches in development (e.g. WVE-003 targeting SNP3) and AAV-delivered miRNA approaches (AMT-130) aim to preserve wild-type HTT function [s2].

citations.title: Tabrizi SJ et al. Targeting Huntingtin Expression in Patients with HD. NEJM 2019
citations.snippet: The HD-causing CAG expansion in HTT produces an N-terminal polyglutamine tract; lowering huntingtin protein is a leading disease-modifying strategy. The investigational antisense oligonucleotide IONIS-HTTRx lowered mutant huntingtin in CSF.

citations.title: GENERATION HD1 tominersen update
citations.snippet: Roche announced in March 2021 that dosing in the GENERATION HD1 phase 3 trial of tominersen would be paused based on benefit/risk assessment; subsequent analyses showed the high-dose arm fared worse than placebo. Allele-selective approaches and AAV-miRNA programs (AMT-130) continue.

answer: Sickle cell disease is caused by homozygous HbS (HBB E6V); under deoxygenation HbS polymerizes and red cells sickle [s1]. Re-inducing fetal hemoglobin (HbF) blocks HbS polymerization and is the rationale for the BCL11A-disrupting therapies. BCL11A is the major postnatal repressor of gamma-globin; in adults, disrupting its erythroid enhancer (the +58 site) de-represses gamma-globin and elevates HbF [s2]. Exa-cel (exagamglogene autotemcel, Casgevy) is an ex vivo CRISPR-Cas9 therapy: hematopoietic stem cells are edited at the BCL11A erythroid enhancer and re-infused [s2]. Casgevy received FDA approval in December 2023 for SCD in patients 12 and older [s3].

citations.title: Bunn HF. Pathogenesis and treatment of sickle cell disease. NEJM 1997
citations.snippet: Hemoglobin S polymerizes upon deoxygenation, distorting the red cell into the characteristic sickled shape and leading to vaso-occlusion.

citations.title: Frangoul H et al. CRISPR-Cas9 Gene Editing for Sickle Cell Disease and Transfusion-Dependent beta-Thalassemia. NEJM 2021
citations.snippet: We used CRISPR-Cas9 to introduce indels at the BCL11A erythroid enhancer in autologous CD34+ hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells, then reinfused the edited cells. Treated patients showed substantial increases in fetal hemoglobin and absence of vaso-occlusive crises.

citations.title: FDA approves first gene therapies to treat patients with sickle cell disease
citations.snippet: On December 8, 2023, the FDA approved two cell-based gene therapies, Casgevy and Lyfgenia, for the treatment of sickle cell disease in patients 12 years of age and older.

answer: Hereditary ATTR amyloidosis is driven by destabilizing TTR variants (e.g. V122I) that promote tetramer dissociation, monomer misfolding, and amyloid deposition in nerves and myocardium [s1]. Hepatic knockdown of TTR removes the substrate for fibril formation. Patisiran (Onpattro) is a lipid-nanoparticle-formulated siRNA targeting TTR mRNA, administered IV every 3 weeks [s1]. Vutrisiran (Amvuttra) is a GalNAc-conjugated siRNA, subcutaneous every 3 months, that achieves comparable TTR knockdown with simpler administration [s2]. Inotersen (Tegsedi) is a TTR-targeting ASO, distinct chemistry from the siRNAs. Investigationally, NTLA-2001 is an in vivo CRISPR-Cas9 therapy that introduces TTR knockout edits in hepatocytes after a single LNP infusion [s3].

citations.title: Adams D et al. Patisiran, an RNAi Therapeutic, for Hereditary Transthyretin Amyloidosis. NEJM 2018
citations.snippet: Patisiran reduced serum transthyretin levels and improved measures of polyneuropathy in patients with hereditary ATTR amyloidosis. ATTRv is caused by destabilizing mutations in TTR that promote tetramer dissociation and amyloid fibril deposition.

citations.title: Adams D et al. Efficacy and safety of vutrisiran for hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis (HELIOS-A). 2022
citations.snippet: Vutrisiran is a subcutaneous GalNAc-conjugated siRNA dosed every three months; HELIOS-A demonstrated noninferior TTR knockdown and improved neuropathy outcomes compared to a patisiran reference.

citations.title: Gillmore JD et al. CRISPR-Cas9 In Vivo Gene Editing for Transthyretin Amyloidosis. NEJM 2021
citations.snippet: NTLA-2001 is an in vivo CRISPR-Cas9 therapy in which guide RNA and Cas9 mRNA are delivered to hepatocytes by lipid nanoparticles; a single infusion produced dose-dependent reductions in serum TTR.

answer: F508del is a class II mutation in CFTR that produces a misfolded protein degraded by ER quality control before reaching the plasma membrane [s1]. The triple-modulator regimen elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor (Trikafta) targets both folding and channel gating. Tezacaftor and elexacaftor are correctors that stabilize CFTR folding and improve trafficking to the apical membrane [s1]. Ivacaftor is a potentiator that increases the open-channel probability of CFTR once at the membrane [s1]. Trikafta is FDA-approved for patients with at least one F508del allele aged 2 and older, and substantially improves FEV1, sweat chloride, and quality of life relative to prior modulators [s2].

citations.title: Heijerman HGM et al. Efficacy and safety of elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor in F508del homozygotes. Lancet 2019
citations.snippet: F508del CFTR is misfolded and retained in the ER. Elexacaftor and tezacaftor act as correctors that improve CFTR processing; ivacaftor potentiates channel opening at the cell surface. Combined, they yielded substantial improvements in FEV1 and sweat chloride.

citations.title: Middleton PG et al. Elexacaftor/Tezacaftor/Ivacaftor for CF with F508del. NEJM 2019
citations.snippet: In patients with cystic fibrosis with a single F508del allele, elexacaftor-tezacaftor-ivacaftor improved FEV1 by 13.8 percentage points and lowered sweat chloride compared with placebo.

answer: Biallelic RPE65 loss-of-function impairs the visual cycle: RPE65 is the RPE-resident isomerase that regenerates 11-cis-retinal, the visual pigment chromophore [s1]. Voretigene neparvovec (Luxturna) is an AAV2 vector carrying human RPE65 cDNA delivered by subretinal injection [s1]. Improvement in functional vision was demonstrated in a phase 3 trial measuring multi-luminance mobility navigation [s1]. Approved by the FDA in December 2017, voretigene was the first directly administered gene therapy in the US. Viable photoreceptors must remain — children typically benefit more than older patients with advanced retinal degeneration [s2].

citations.title: Russell S et al. Efficacy and safety of voretigene neparvovec (AAV2-hRPE65v2) in patients with RPE65-mediated inherited retinal dystrophy. Lancet 2017
citations.snippet: Voretigene neparvovec is an adeno-associated virus serotype 2 vector encoding human RPE65 delivered by subretinal injection. Treated patients showed significant improvement on the multi-luminance mobility test.

citations.title: FDA Luxturna information
citations.snippet: Luxturna is indicated for biallelic RPE65 mutation-associated retinal dystrophy in patients with viable retinal cells. FDA-approved December 2017.

answer: Heterozygous LDLR loss-of-function reduces hepatic LDL receptor density and elevates LDL-C [s1]. PCSK9 binds the LDL receptor and targets it for lysosomal degradation; inhibiting PCSK9 increases LDLR recycling and lowers LDL-C even further on top of statins [s1]. Three approved PCSK9-directed therapies should be considered: evolocumab (Repatha) and alirocumab (Praluent) — both subcutaneous monoclonal antibodies dosed every 2 weeks [s1]; and inclisiran (Leqvio), a hepatocyte-targeted siRNA dosed twice yearly [s2]. The FOURIER trial (evolocumab) and ODYSSEY OUTCOMES (alirocumab) showed cardiovascular event reductions [s1].

citations.title: Sabatine MS et al. Evolocumab and Clinical Outcomes in Patients with Cardiovascular Disease (FOURIER). NEJM 2017
citations.snippet: PCSK9 binds the hepatic LDL receptor and promotes its lysosomal degradation. Inhibition of PCSK9 with evolocumab in patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease reduced LDL cholesterol and the risk of cardiovascular events.

citations.title: Ray KK et al. Two Phase 3 Trials of Inclisiran in Patients with Elevated LDL Cholesterol. NEJM 2020
citations.snippet: Inclisiran, a hepatocyte-targeted siRNA against PCSK9, reduced LDL cholesterol by approximately 50% with twice-yearly subcutaneous dosing.

answer: Hereditary angioedema type 1 results from SERPING1 haploinsufficiency: reduced C1-INH function leaves plasma kallikrein unrestrained, generating bradykinin from high-molecular-weight kininogen [s1]. Bradykinin acts on endothelial B2 receptors causing the characteristic vascular leak. Long-term prophylaxis is the standard for frequent attacks. Lanadelumab (Takhzyro) is a subcutaneous monoclonal antibody against plasma kallikrein dosed every 2-4 weeks [s2]. Berotralstat (Orladeyo) is an oral plasma kallikrein inhibitor for daily prophylaxis [s3]. For on-demand treatment, sebetralstat (Ekterly) was approved in 2025 as the first oral on-demand plasma kallikrein inhibitor [s4]. Investigationally, NTLA-2002 is an in vivo CRISPR-Cas9 therapy targeting hepatic KLKB1 [s5].

citations.title: Zuraw BL. Hereditary angioedema. NEJM 2008
citations.snippet: In hereditary angioedema, deficient C1-inhibitor function permits unchecked activation of plasma kallikrein. Plasma kallikrein cleaves high-molecular-weight kininogen to release bradykinin, which acts on B2 receptors to cause vascular permeability.

citations.title: Banerji A et al. Effect of Lanadelumab in Hereditary Angioedema (HELP). JAMA 2018
citations.snippet: Lanadelumab, a fully human monoclonal antibody inhibiting active plasma kallikrein, reduced the rate of hereditary angioedema attacks compared with placebo.

citations.title: Zuraw B et al. Oral Berotralstat for Prophylactic Treatment of Hereditary Angioedema (APeX-2). JACI 2020
citations.snippet: Berotralstat is an oral, once-daily plasma kallikrein inhibitor that reduced hereditary angioedema attack rates over 24 weeks.

citations.title: FDA approves Ekterly (sebetralstat) for on-demand HAE treatment
citations.snippet: Sebetralstat is the first oral on-demand therapy approved for hereditary angioedema attacks; it inhibits plasma kallikrein.

citations.title: Cohn DM et al. CRISPR-based therapy (NTLA-2002) for hereditary angioedema. NEJM 2024
citations.snippet: NTLA-2002 is an in vivo CRISPR-Cas9 therapy that knocks out KLKB1 in hepatocytes; a single dose reduced plasma kallikrein activity and angioedema attack rates in a phase 1/2 trial.
